The input is ready. Before I run the deconvolution, I need two answers from you:

**1. CIBERSORTx (CBSX) credentials.** CBSX is one of multideconv's default methods, along with Quantiseq, EpiDISH, DeconRNASeq and DWLS. It only runs with a CIBERSORTx account. Do you have your CIBERSORTx **email and API token**? If you don't, you can register for free at https://cibersortx.stanford.edu and generate a token there. Then pick one:
- **(a)** Run now without CBSX. The other four methods still run; CBSX would only add one more method to cross-check the estimates against.
- **(b)** Wait until you have the credentials, then run with CBSX included.

**2. Custom signatures.** Do you have any pre-computed signature files (for example, melanoma-specific references) that should be used alongside the bundled ones? If so, tell me where they are.

Here's what I found in the data so far:
- **Scale:** `Gide_log2TPM.txt` holds log2(TPM+1): 18,979 genes × 73 samples, values 0–14, no negatives or NAs. Deconvolution needs linear TPM, so I converted it back (2^x − 1) and saved it to `results/input/Gide_TPM_linear.csv`. It will be run with `normalized=False`.
- **Clinical data:** All 73 samples match the Gide rows of `colData_all.txt`: 41 anti-PD1 (22 responders, 19 non-responders) and 32 ipilimumab+anti-PD1 (24 responders, 8 non-responders), all pre-treatment. That subset is saved in `results/input/Gide_coldata.csv`.
- **One odd sample:** `8_PD1_PRE` has an unusually low total TPM (~41k against a median of ~510k). Its expression profile still matches the rest of the cohort closely (Spearman 0.93), so I plan to keep it and mark it in the results.

# Immune / stromal composition and immune-infiltration ranking for the Gide cohort,
# built from multideconv output (results/01_deconvolution, results/02_harmonized_subgroups).
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ggplot2); library(tidyr); library(dplyr); library(ComplexHeatmap); library(circlize)
})
setwd("/home/marcelo.hurtado/Documents/tme_analysis/0760e3f28f/work")
out <- "results/03_immune_infiltration"; dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

raw  <- read.csv("results/01_deconvolution/result.csv", row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
harm <- read.csv("results/02_harmonized_subgroups/result_Deconvolution.matrix.csv", row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
cd   <- read.csv("results/input/Gide_coldata.csv", row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
# R prefixed sample names starting with a digit with "X": restore the original IDs
fix_ids <- function(x) sub("^X(?=[0-9])", "", x, perl = TRUE)
rownames(raw) <- fix_ids(rownames(raw)); rownames(harm) <- fix_ids(rownames(harm))
stopifnot(setequal(rownames(raw), rownames(cd)), identical(rownames(raw), rownames(harm)))

# ---- Compartment annotation of every method_signature_celltype feature ----
parts  <- strsplit(colnames(raw), "_")
combo  <- sapply(parts, function(z) paste(z[1:2], collapse = "_"))
ctype  <- sapply(parts, function(z) paste(z[-(1:2)], collapse = "_"))
stromal_types <- c("Endothelial", "CAF", "Fibroblasts", "Myocytes", "Mural.cells", "Pericytes")
tumor_types   <- c("Cancer", "Epithelial", "uncharacterized.cell")
compartment <- ifelse(ctype %in% stromal_types, "Stromal",
               ifelse(ctype %in% tumor_types, "Tumor/other", "Immune"))
lineage <- case_when(
  compartment == "Stromal" & ctype == "Endothelial" ~ "Endothelial",
  compartment == "Stromal" ~ "Fibroblasts/CAF/mural",
  compartment == "Tumor/other" ~ "Tumor/other",
  grepl("^CD4|^CD8|^T\\.cells|^NKT", ctype) ~ "T cells",
  grepl("^B\\.|^Plasma", ctype) ~ "B/plasma cells",
  grepl("^NK", ctype) ~ "NK cells",
  TRUE ~ "Myeloid cells")
annot <- data.frame(feature = colnames(raw), combo, cell_type = ctype, compartment, lineage)
write.csv(annot, file.path(out, "feature_compartment_annotation.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Only combinations whose signature includes non-immune compartments can measure infiltration
# (in immune-only signatures such as LM22 the immune fractions always sum to 1).
informative <- unique(annot$combo[annot$compartment != "Immune"])
frac_by <- function(comp) sapply(informative, function(cb) {
  cols <- annot$feature[annot$combo == cb & annot$compartment == comp]
  if (length(cols) == 0) return(rep(NA_real_, nrow(raw)))
  rowSums(raw[, cols, drop = FALSE])
})
immune  <- frac_by("Immune");  rownames(immune)  <- rownames(raw)
stromal <- frac_by("Stromal"); rownames(stromal) <- rownames(raw)
stromal <- stromal[, colSums(!is.na(stromal)) > 0, drop = FALSE]
write.csv(immune,  file.path(out, "immune_fraction_per_method_signature.csv"))
write.csv(stromal, file.path(out, "stromal_fraction_per_method_signature.csv"))

# Cross-method agreement on the immune fraction
agree <- cor(immune, method = "spearman")
write.csv(agree, file.path(out, "immune_fraction_cross_method_spearman.csv"))
pdf(file.path(out, "immune_fraction_cross_method_agreement.pdf"), width = 9, height = 8)
draw(Heatmap(agree, name = "Spearman", col = colorRamp2(c(-1, 0, 1), c("#2166AC", "white", "#B2182B")),
             column_title = "Agreement of total immune fraction across method x signature",
             cell_fun = function(j, i, x, y, w, h, f) grid.text(sprintf("%.2f", agree[i, j]), x, y, gp = gpar(fontsize = 6))))
dev.off()

# ---- Consensus scores: mean of per-combination z-scores (scale-free across methods) ----
consensus <- function(m) rowMeans(scale(m), na.rm = TRUE)
res <- data.frame(
  Sample = rownames(raw),
  Immune_score = consensus(immune),
  Immune_fraction_median = apply(immune, 1, median),
  Immune_fraction_IQR_low = apply(immune, 1, quantile, 0.25),
  Immune_fraction_IQR_high = apply(immune, 1, quantile, 0.75),
  Stromal_score = consensus(stromal),
  Stromal_fraction_median = apply(stromal, 1, median),
  Methods_agreeing_high = rowSums(sweep(immune, 2, apply(immune, 2, median), ">")) # n combos above their cohort median
)
res$Immune_rank <- rank(-res$Immune_score)
tert <- quantile(res$Immune_score, c(1/3, 2/3))
res$Infiltration_group <- factor(ifelse(res$Immune_score > tert[2], "High",
                                 ifelse(res$Immune_score <= tert[1], "Low", "Intermediate")),
                                 levels = c("High", "Intermediate", "Low"))
res <- cbind(res, cd[res$Sample, c("Therapy", "Response")])
res$Note <- ifelse(res$Sample == "8_PD1_PRE", "low total TPM in input matrix (~41k)", "")
res <- res[order(res$Immune_rank), ]
write.csv(res, file.path(out, "immune_infiltration_ranking.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# ---- Lineage composition per patient (median across informative combos, renormalized) ----
lin_levels <- c("T cells", "B/plasma cells", "NK cells", "Myeloid cells", "Endothelial", "Fibroblasts/CAF/mural", "Tumor/other")
lin <- sapply(lin_levels, function(l) {
  per_combo <- sapply(informative, function(cb) {
    cols <- annot$feature[annot$combo == cb & annot$lineage == l]
    if (length(cols) == 0) NA_real_ else rowSums(raw[, cols, drop = FALSE])
  })
  apply(matrix(per_combo, nrow = nrow(raw)), 1, median, na.rm = TRUE)
})
rownames(lin) <- rownames(raw); lin[is.na(lin)] <- 0
lin <- lin / rowSums(lin)
write.csv(lin, file.path(out, "lineage_composition_consensus.csv"))

ord <- res$Sample
lin_long <- as.data.frame(lin) %>% mutate(Sample = rownames(lin)) %>%
  pivot_longer(-Sample, names_to = "Lineage", values_to = "Fraction") %>%
  mutate(Sample = factor(Sample, levels = ord), Lineage = factor(Lineage, levels = rev(lin_levels)))
pal <- c("T cells" = "#D7301F", "B/plasma cells" = "#FC8D59", "NK cells" = "#FDCC8A", "Myeloid cells" = "#7B3294",
         "Endothelial" = "#1A9850", "Fibroblasts/CAF/mural" = "#91CF60", "Tumor/other" = "#BDBDBD")
grp_bounds <- cumsum(table(res$Infiltration_group))[1:2] + 0.5
p1 <- ggplot(lin_long, aes(Sample, Fraction, fill = Lineage)) + geom_col(width = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = grp_bounds, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal) + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(title = "Gide cohort: consensus TME composition (median across 13 method x signature combinations)",
       subtitle = "Patients ordered by consensus immune score (High | Intermediate | Low tertiles)", x = NULL, y = "Fraction") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 10) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 6))
ggsave(file.path(out, "lineage_composition_stacked.pdf"), p1, width = 14, height = 5.5)

p2 <- ggplot(res, aes(reorder(Sample, -Immune_score), Immune_fraction_median, colour = Infiltration_group)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = Immune_fraction_IQR_low, ymax = Immune_fraction_IQR_high), size = 0.25) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(High = "#B2182B", Intermediate = "#F4A582", Low = "#4393C3")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(title = "Total immune fraction per patient", subtitle = "Median and IQR across the 13 method x signature combinations",
       x = NULL, y = "Immune fraction", colour = "Infiltration") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 10) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 6))

tumor_types   <- c("Cancer", "Epithelial", "uncharacterized.cell")
compartment <- ifelse(ctype %in% stromal_types, "Stromal",
               ifelse(ctype %in% tumor_types, "Tumor/other", "Immune"))
lineage <- case_when(
  compartment == "Stromal" & ctype == "Endothelial" ~ "Endothelial",
  compartment == "Stromal" ~ "Fibroblasts/CAF/mural",
  compartment == "Tumor/other" ~ "Tumor/other",
  grepl("^CD4|^CD8|^T\\.cells|^NKT", ctype) ~ "T cells",
  grepl("^B\\.|^Plasma", ctype) ~ "B/plasma cells",
  grepl("^NK", ctype) ~ "NK cells",
  TRUE ~ "Myeloid cells")
annot <- data.frame(feature = colnames(raw), combo, cell_type = ctype, compartment, lineage)
write.csv(annot, file.path(out, "feature_compartment_annotation.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

frac_by <- function(comp) sapply(informative, function(cb) {
  cols <- annot$feature[annot$combo == cb & annot$compartment == comp]
  if (length(cols) == 0) return(rep(NA_real_, nrow(raw)))
  rowSums(raw[, cols, drop = FALSE])
})

write.csv(stromal, file.path(out, "stromal_fraction_per_method_signature.csv"))

content.text:
The multideconv deconvolution of all 73 Gide samples is done. 24 patients come out as highly immune infiltrated, 24 as intermediate and 25 as low. Everything is saved in `results/`.

**What went into it**
- Your file holds log2(TPM+1), so I converted it back to linear TPM (2^x − 1) for deconvolution.
- I ran 5 methods (Quantiseq, EpiDISH, DeconRNASeq, DWLS and CIBERSORTx) with 7 signatures, giving 375 raw estimates.
- multideconv reduced these to 194 consensus features. It dropped 41 that were zero in more than 90% of samples, mostly some NK, CD8, Treg and neutrophil estimates.

**How I defined "immune infiltrated"**
- Only 13 of the method×signature combinations also estimate tumor or stromal cells, so only they can say how much of a sample is immune. The rest only estimate immune cells, so they can't.
- For each patient I took the total immune fraction from each of those 13 combinations and averaged the standardized values into one immune score.
- I then split patients into thirds: High, Intermediate and Low.
- The methods agree well on who ranks high or low (median Spearman correlation 0.65).
- They disagree on absolute levels: the cohort-median immune fraction ranges from 11% to 71% depending on the combination. So rely on the ranking, not any single percentage.

**Composition** (melanoma-specific signature, the most realistic absolute numbers; cohort median)

| Cell type | Median fraction |
|---|---|
| Tumor cells | ~51% |
| Fibroblasts (CAF) | ~19% |
| Macrophages | ~10% |
| CD4 T cells | ~3% |
| Endothelial cells | ~2% |
| NK cells | <1% |
| B cells | <1% |
| CD8 T cells | ~0% (Q3 ~1%) |

- **Macrophages are the largest immune population.** All lymphocyte types together are much smaller.
- **More immune means less stroma.** The immune and stromal scores are negatively correlated (Spearman −0.65). Low-infiltrated tumors have about twice the fibroblast fraction of high ones (median 38% vs 16%).
- **Fibroblasts are probably overestimated in the all-signature consensus.** Its median stromal fraction is ~43%, because the non-melanoma signatures have no melanoma tumor reference and count melanoma cells as fibroblasts.

**Most immune-infiltrated patients** (high third, ordered by score):
20_ipiPD1, 13_ipiPD1, 37_ipiPD1, 7_PD1, 45_PD1, 6_PD1, 53_PD1, 32_ipiPD1, 40_PD1, 44_PD1, 21_ipiPD1, 38_PD1, 48_PD1, 47_PD1, 27_ipiPD1, 54_PD1, 26_ipiPD1, 36_PD1, 46_ipiPD1, 47_ipiPD1, 34_PD1, 24_ipiPD1, 21_PD1, 36_ipiPD1 (all `_PRE`).
- The top three stand out, with a median of 74–90% immune content across combinations.
- The least infiltrated include 42_PD1, 45_ipiPD1, 16_PD1, 3_PD1, 25_ipiPD1 and 13_PD1, each around 9–17% immune.
- High-infiltrated tumors have more macrophages (15% vs 7%), CD4 T cells (5% vs 2%) and CD8 T cells than low ones.

**Things to be aware of**
- **Sample `8_PD1_PRE`** has an unusually low total TPM in your input file. Its expression profile still matches the cohort, so I kept it. It ranks Low (57th of 73), and it is flagged in the ranking table.
- **Your CIBERSORTx token is stored in plain text** in `results/01_deconvolution/manifest.json`. The exported session log masks it. Remove or redact that file before sharing `results/`.
- I added each patient's therapy and response as reference columns in the ranking table, but I did not test any link between infiltration and response.

**Files in `results/`**
- `input/`: the linear TPM matrix and the Gide clinical subset.
- `01_deconvolution/`: raw multideconv output (375 features).
- `02_harmonized_subgroups/`: consensus cell subgroups and lists of discarded features.
- `03_immune_infiltration/`:
  - `immune_infiltration_ranking.csv`: the main table, with score, rank, group, immune fraction (median and IQR) and stromal score per patient.
  - Composition tables and stacked bar charts.
  - Per-method immune and stromal fractions, plus a heatmap of how well the methods agree.
  - A heatmap of the 194 consensus features with patients ordered by immune score.
- `scripts/immune_infiltration.R`: the code that builds the score, tables and plots.
- `session_export/`: the reproducibility log.

If useful, I could next test whether the infiltration groups or individual cell types differ between responders and non-responders.
